takeaways: **Takeaway:** in all five v2 datasets, the share of questions with several correct answers is low. After adjudication it is 1.0% for SimpleQA, 0% for BrowseComp, 3.0% for HLE, 4.0% for TriviaQA and 5.5% for WebInstruct-verified, and every upper 95% bound is below 10%. That is close to v1's math sets (0-2.5%) and far below v1's NQ-open (30%). SimpleQA and TriviaQA questions were written to have one answer, and BrowseComp questions stack constraints until one answer remains, so the low rates fit how these sets were built. NQ-open questions are real search queries.

**The two annotators agree much less than v1's two Claude passes did.** Kappa (3-class) runs from 0.00 (BrowseComp) to 0.29 (TriviaQA). Most of the gap is not about MULTI. Sonnet 5 applies the UNCLEAR clause "cannot be decided without deep solving" to hard lookup and research questions (187/200 on BrowseComp, 98/200 on HLE), while GPT-5-mini labels the same items UNIQUE because the constraints seem to pin down one answer. When Opus 5 adjudicated such cases, it chose UNIQUE in all 79 BrowseComp cases and in 40 of 48 HLE cases.

**On MULTI itself, GPT-5-mini is far more willing than Sonnet 5**: 14.5% versus 1.5% on HLE, 17.5% versus 5.0% on WebInstruct, and 7.5% versus 2.0% on TriviaQA. The adjudicator accepted few MULTI labels that only GPT-5-mini gave: 4 of 22 adjudicated on HLE, 2 of 26 on WebInstruct, and 4 of 12 on TriviaQA. That is why the range between the lower bound (both annotators say MULTI) and the upper bound (either says MULTI) is wide: 4.5% to 18.0% on WebInstruct, 1.0% to 15.0% on HLE, 1.5% to 8.0% on TriviaQA. The rates reported above depend on the adjudicator, so cite them with that range.

**The adjudicator did not simply side with Sonnet 5, the other Claude model.** Opus 5 sided with GPT-5-mini in 22 of 24 SimpleQA, 79 of 79 BrowseComp and 45 of 71 HLE adjudications, and with Sonnet 5 in 35 of 46 WebInstruct and 9 of 13 TriviaQA adjudications.

**Which kinds of MULTI appear:** open-domain MULTI cases are mostly different correct entities (Tudor also made a Submariner watch; Ricky Hatton was also 'The Hitman') or answers that changed over time (TriviaQA 3 of 8). Math and science MULTI cases are unpinned readings (which risk-free rate, when a benefit arrives, how to read '6% of vaccinated') or open requests ('find a basis', 'what are some ideas', 'find n such that').
v1_takeaways: **The v1 results mostly hold up under a different model family.** Pooled over the 800 v1 items, GPT-5-mini agrees with v1's final Claude labels 88.8% of the time, with kappa 0.55 [0.46, 0.62] over 3 classes and 0.53 [0.44, 0.61] for MULTI versus rest. GPT-5-mini found 9 of v1's 10 math MULTI items (GSM8K 4 of 5, missing only gsm8k-1254; DeepScaleR 5 of 5) and 48 of v1's 60 NQ-open MULTI items. The 12 NQ-open items it missed are 5 temporal, 4 multiple-entity and 3 ambiguous-reading.

**Most of the disagreement is GPT-5-mini adding MULTI labels that v1 did not give**, the same pattern as in v2. MATH-500: 5 versus 0. GSM8K: 13 versus 5. DeepScaleR: 21 versus 5. NQ-open: 87 versus 60. So v1's rates look more like a lower estimate than an inflated one, but this comparison sets one unadjudicated annotator against adjudicated final labels.
MATH-500 kappa is 0 even with 97.5% raw agreement: v1 labeled every MATH-500 item UNIQUE, so any MULTI label from GPT-5-mini (5 items) drives chance-corrected agreement to 0.
failures: **Anthropic cap reached during adjudication.** Recorded spend is $11.86; the next worst-case reservation would have passed $12, so it was refused. SimpleQA (24), TriviaQA (13) and WebInstruct (46) were fully adjudicated. BrowseComp got 79 of 185 adjudications. HLE got 71 of 100: 24 were not reached before the cap, and 5 failed after 3 attempts (4 hit the 800-token limit without a JSON object, 1 was refused). The remaining 106 BrowseComp and 29 HLE items took the pre-registered fallback label.

**Effect of the fallbacks.** All 106 BrowseComp fallbacks are UNCLEAR-vs-UNIQUE pairs, which the rule turns into UNCLEAR. So BrowseComp's 108 UNCLEAR are mostly an artifact of the cap: every one of the 79 adjudicated BrowseComp disagreements ended UNIQUE. BrowseComp's MULTI count cannot change, because neither annotator labeled any BrowseComp item MULTI. Of the 29 HLE fallbacks, 6 involve a MULTI label. If all 6 had been adjudicated MULTI, HLE would be 12/200 = 6.0% [3.5, 10.2], the most the cap could hide.

**Pass A refusal.** Sonnet 5 refused one HLE item (hle-66fc2df0b72463921f6c40f2, Biology/Medicine) on all 3 attempts. The item went to adjudication, Opus 5 refused it too, and the fallback gave it Pass B's label (UNIQUE). Pass B had no failures; OpenAI spend stayed well under its cap.
All five datasets downloaded and decrypted or filtered as specified. No dataset was substituted.
Kappa notes: SimpleQA's MULTI-versus-rest kappa is 0 because GPT-5-mini labeled no SimpleQA item MULTI. BrowseComp's is undefined because neither annotator labeled any item MULTI.
limitations: All labels come from LLMs, not humans, and no model had web search. Open-domain alternatives rest on model knowledge. The orchestrating Claude session that checked the examples is also an LLM.

The adjudicator (Claude Opus 5) shares a developer with Pass A (Claude Sonnet 5). The adjudication pattern above shows no simple same-family preference, but correlated blind spots cannot be ruled out.

Chance-corrected agreement between the passes is low (kappa 0.00-0.35), so the final MULTI rates depend on one adjudicator model. The lower and upper bounds (both / either annotator MULTI) are the conservative way to cite them.
On HLE and BrowseComp the UNCLEAR definition was read very differently by the two annotators, so UNCLEAR counts there are unreliable. MULTI counts are less affected.
The Anthropic cap left 106 BrowseComp and 29 HLE disagreements unadjudicated. The fallback rule can only lower MULTI, and its largest possible effect on HLE is stated above.
HLE is restricted to text-only exact-match items (1645 of 2500). Multiple-choice and image items are not covered.

Several MULTI examples look questionable on inspection. Some are reference errors rather than several valid answers (hle-672db430: enumeration gives 4 wallpaper groups against a reference of 3; simpleqa-1432). Others ask for something different from what the reference answers (webinstruct-53602 asks for points, the reference is a distance). Some describe one set at a different granularity (webinstruct-129388). Under the protocol these are reported as checks and do not change labels, so the final MULTI counts may slightly overstate true multiplicity.
